issues.title: Bootstrap PostgreSQL, Prisma, and environment validation
issues.summary: Set up the production data foundation for the server-backed app, including database connectivity, Prisma wiring, and validated environment configuration.
sourceSections: Immediate Next Step For The Next Agent
scope: Add Prisma and PostgreSQL project dependencies.
Establish environment variable loading and validation for database configuration.
Document the local setup needed to run database-backed development.
acceptanceCriteria: The project has a documented PostgreSQL and Prisma setup path for local development.
Environment variables required for database access are validated before app startup.
The repository is ready for follow-up schema and migration work.
openQuestions: Choose the environment validation approach that best matches the app's future server runtime.

issues.title: Define the initial Prisma schema and baseline migrations
issues.summary: Model the first production-ready database schema around users, families, recipes, meal plans, shopping items, and stores.
sourceSections: Immediate Next Step For The Next Agent
scope: Define the first Prisma models for the core entities called out in the summary.
Add baseline migrations for the initial schema.
Keep the schema extensible for future meal types and collaboration metadata.
acceptanceCriteria: Core entities from the summary exist in the Prisma schema with appropriate relations.
The first migration can be applied to a clean database.
The schema design preserves server-backed ownership of meal planning and shopping state.
openQuestions: Confirm whether stores should be global, family-scoped, or both before finalizing nullability rules.

issues.title: Seed starter recipes, ingredient categories, and store sections
issues.summary: Add seed data that supports early development and provides realistic fixtures for planning and shopping flows.
scope: Seed a useful starter set of recipes and ingredient categories.
Seed store section defaults that support shopping list ordering.
Keep the seeded data easy to extend as the production model evolves.
acceptanceCriteria: A fresh development database can be seeded with meaningful starter data.
Seeded recipes and categories are sufficient to exercise meal planning and shopping flows.
Store section data can be reused by later shopping and store-mode work.

issues.title: Add authentication, session handling, and protected routes
issues.summary: Introduce the first login/session flow and route protection so production features can move off the prototype safely.
sourceSections: Core Workflows To Implement > 1. Authentication and family onboarding
Immediate Next Step For The Next Agent
scope: Choose and implement the initial auth/session strategy.
Protect production routes behind authenticated access.
Keep user-facing text Norwegian while wiring the first auth UI.
acceptanceCriteria: A user can register or sign in using the chosen initial auth flow.
Server routes can determine the current user from session state.
Protected routes redirect or reject unauthenticated access.
openQuestions: The summary allows either password-based or external auth fields, so the initial auth strategy needs a concrete choice.

issues.title: Build family onboarding with create-family and join-code flows
issues.summary: Implement the first family collaboration entry point so authenticated users can create or join a family before planning meals.
sourceSections: Core Workflows To Implement > 1. Authentication and family onboarding
scope: Let a signed-in user create a family and become its first admin.
Let a signed-in user join an existing family by unique code.
Add the first protected family dashboard or landing state.
acceptanceCriteria: Users can create a family and are persisted as admin members.
Users can join a family by code through a protected flow.
The app has a family-scoped landing route ready for meal plan work.
openQuestions: Clarify whether a user can belong to multiple families before broadening the membership UX.

issues.title: Add family membership management and authorization boundaries
issues.summary: Define who can do what inside a family and implement the first admin-only member management capabilities.
sourceSections: Core Workflows To Implement > 1. Authentication and family onboarding
scope: Add role-aware authorization for family member versus family admin actions.
Implement the first admin-facing member management behavior needed after onboarding.
Cover authorization boundaries with focused automated tests.
acceptanceCriteria: Family-scoped actions enforce admin versus member permissions.
Admins can perform the initial member-management actions defined for the first release.
Authorization boundaries are covered by targeted tests.
openQuestions: The summary mentions administrator permissions, but the exact permission matrix still needs product clarification.

issues.title: Implement meal plan CRUD with date-range validation
issues.summary: Create the first real meal plan workflow with persisted start and end dates, family ownership, and the initial 7-day cap.
sourceSections: Core Workflows To Implement > 2. Meal plan lifecycle
Immediate Next Step For The Next Agent
scope: Allow families to create, list, select, update, and delete meal plans.
Enforce explicit startDate and endDate handling with a maximum initial span of 7 days.
Preserve support for partial active weeks such as Thursday through Sunday.
acceptanceCriteria: Families can manage meal plans with persisted start and end dates.
Date-range validation rejects invalid or overlong ranges and is covered by tests.
The first production meal plan routes are backed by server data rather than local storage.

issues.title: Implement daily meal plan entry editing for dinner-first planning
issues.summary: Add the core day-by-day planning workflow so a family can attach recipes or notes to dates inside a meal plan.
sourceSections: Core Workflows To Implement > 2. Meal plan lifecycle
scope: Support editing meal plan entries per active date.
Start with dinner as the main meal type while keeping the schema extensible.
Allow recipe selection and entry notes in the first production flow.
acceptanceCriteria: Users can assign dinners to dates within the active meal plan.
The entry model is ready for future meal-type expansion without rework.
The production flow mirrors the validated prototype behavior for the initial planning journey.

issues.title: Implement meal plan copy and reuse into a new date range
issues.summary: Support reusing a previous meal plan as a starting point while respecting the selected target date range.
sourceSections: Core Workflows To Implement > 2. Meal plan lifecycle
scope: Add a copy or reuse action from an existing meal plan.
Map entries into a newly selected target date range.
Define what data is copied now versus intentionally left behind.
acceptanceCriteria: Users can create a new meal plan from an existing one.
Copied plans respect the new date range and preserve expected entries.
Copy behavior is covered by focused automated tests.
openQuestions: Clarify whether manual shopping items, notes, and approval state are copied or reset.

issues.title: Add meal plan approval state and guarded transitions
issues.summary: Introduce an explicit approval step so families can confirm a plan before shopping and calendar workflows depend on it.
sourceSections: Core Workflows To Implement > 2. Meal plan lifecycle
scope: Persist draft versus approved state on meal plans.
Define who can approve a plan and what transitions are allowed.
Guard downstream actions as needed based on approval state.
acceptanceCriteria: Meal plans can move between the supported workflow states.
Approval actions enforce the chosen authorization and transition rules.
The implementation leaves room for stricter locking rules later.
openQuestions: The summary does not yet define whether approval locks further edits or just marks the plan as confirmed.

issues.title: Build deterministic shopping list projection from meal plan recipes
issues.summary: Generate shopping list items from planned recipes on the server so the list stays reproducible and auditable.
sourceSections: Core Workflows To Implement > 3. Shopping list generation
scope: Derive generated shopping items from meal plan entries and recipe ingredients.
Keep the generation logic deterministic and server-side.
Cover merge and projection behavior with focused tests.
acceptanceCriteria: The app can project generated shopping items from the current meal plan.
Projection logic is deterministic and does not depend on client-side local storage.
Shopping generation behavior is covered by automated tests.
openQuestions: Ingredient merge rules still need product clarification for differing units, names, and store preferences.

issues.title: Add manual shopping items and persisted override state
issues.summary: Layer user-controlled shopping behavior on top of generated items without losing deterministic regeneration.
sourceSections: Core Workflows To Implement > 3. Shopping list generation
scope: Persist manual shopping items alongside generated projections.
Persist checked state, postponement, notes, and preferred store overrides.
Merge manual and generated items into the user-facing shopping list.
acceptanceCriteria: Users can add manual items to a meal plan shopping list.
User override state survives regeneration of generated shopping items.
Postponement and checked-state behavior are covered by targeted tests.
openQuestions: The exact identity strategy for generated items and `sourceKey` should be nailed down before implementation.

issues.title: Implement store configuration, section ordering, and mobile store mode
issues.summary: Make the shopping list practical in the store by supporting store-specific ordering and a compact mobile-first shopping experience.
sourceSections: Core Workflows To Implement > 4. Store mode
scope: Support store definitions and section ordering per store.
Filter the shopping experience by active shopping date and selected store.
Build the first compact mobile-first store mode UI.
acceptanceCriteria: Users can choose an active store and see items grouped in store order.
Store mode shows only the items relevant for the selected shopping date.
Store ordering behavior is covered by focused automated tests.
openQuestions: The summary leaves open whether store definitions are family-specific, global, or mixed.

issues.title: Add server-side day and meal-plan calendar exports
issues.summary: Expose `.ics` endpoints and UI actions so families can export one day or an entire meal plan to their calendars.
sourceSections: Core Workflows To Implement > 5. Calendar export
scope: Add the initial server-generated `.ics` endpoints for a whole meal plan and a single day.
Add UI entry points for the supported export actions.
Include the planned title, date, and recipe description in the exported events.
acceptanceCriteria: Families can export a whole meal plan or a single day as `.ics`.
Calendar export logic stays server-side.
Export output is covered by correctness tests.
openQuestions: Clarify whether draft plans should be exportable or whether exports should depend on approval.

issues.title: Add collaboration hardening, audit metadata, and conflict safeguards
issues.summary: Strengthen multi-user behavior so shared family planning remains trustworthy as concurrent edits become more common.
scope: Add actor-aware timestamps or equivalent audit-friendly metadata to key write flows.
Handle or surface conflicting edits to shared planning and shopping state.
Improve observability around important writes and failures.
acceptanceCriteria: Key collaborative writes record enough metadata to support audits.
Concurrent edit risks are handled or surfaced intentionally in core workflows.
The implementation improves confidence in shared family usage.
openQuestions: The summary asks for conflict handling and audit support, but the exact strategy still needs to be chosen.
